claims.text: Greg Short asserts that founders should hire specifically to cover the areas they are weakest at and least enjoy, because a founder who spends time on tasks they dislike is less effective than a specialist hired for those tasks, and hiring for pain points prevents burnout by keeping the founder focused on work they find energizing.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.mechanism: Doing tasks you dislike drains energy and accelerates burnout; delegating them to specialists keeps the founder in their zone of enjoyment, sustaining higher output and longevity.

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that between two competing founders in the same market, the one who genuinely enjoys the work will outperform the one who does not, because passion-aligned work produces sustained effort that displaces a less-motivated competitor over time.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.mechanism: Enjoyment of the work produces discretionary effort that compounds over time; the disengaged competitor cannot sustain the same volume or quality of output.

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that the American ideal of building a business around one's passion is not a myth; founders who work in areas they are passionate about have a structural competitive advantage over those who do not.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: the American dream of building a business about what you're passionate about

practices.text: Hire for your pain points — the tasks you are worst at and dislike most — so that each team member covers your gaps and you remain focused on what energizes you.
